summary: A first-person fiction excerpt (Book 2, part 196) in which the narrator receives a text from Checker, newly back in LA, inviting them to a drink. The narrator feels surreal distance from the idea of a sociable life, reflects on a recent visit from Arthur, and softens toward the idea that people are not all bad. The narrator replies accepting, with a dry condition about their new Colt 1911, and signs off as Cas.
one_line: The narrator, Cas, accepts a drinking invitation from Checker after a text arrives, weighing solitude against the possibility of connection.
key_facts: The narrator's phone beeped with a text message from Checker, who had newly arrived back in LA.
The narrator describes a strange, fizzy feeling in their chest when reading the messages.
The invitation feels surreal to the narrator, as if watching someone else's life.
The narrator contrasts themselves with someone who lives in society, makes friends, and goes out drinking with them.
The narrator's texts are usually about work or death threats.
The narrator recalls Arthur's visit while considering the invitation.
The narrator thinks maybe people weren't all bad, at least not all the time.
The narrator thinks it might not be such an awful thing not to drink alone tonight.
The narrator replies to Checker that the invitation works as long as their new Colt 1911 counts.
The narrator's reply ends with 'See you at 8' and is signed 'Cas'.
